conditions: The first rule concerns objects created by declarations in the master that qualify for finalization. The second concerns finalization of a collection associated with a nonderived access type.
limitations: The reverse-order rule is not a universal rule for objects within an access-type collection or for components of one composite object. Explicit deallocation and object accessibility have separate conditions.
Exact unannotated Ada 2022 manual edition only. Runtime implementations and other editions require separate evidence.

triggers: Controlling edition erratum, confirmed online-to-printed discrepancy, exact artifact drift, or contrary applicable evidence.

statement: In the Ada 2022 Reference Manual, a master finalizes eligible objects created by declarations in that master in reverse creation order. The manual separately leaves the order of finalizing objects within an access-type collection arbitrary.
